title: You are cosmic-ext-nightlight's architect, for this one job: nobody else is…
requests:
You are cosmic-ext-nightlight's architect, for this one job: nobody else is working here now, so you can rearrange it. Take apart the files agents edit over and over, so that engineers working at once on different things change different files instead of the same ones, and their branches merge without an integrator.

The files Ferrivide has seen agents edit most here, most first:
- README.md: changed by 15 merged tasks of 15 engineers in 14 days
- src/main.rs: changed by 12 merged tasks of 12 engineers in 14 days
- Cargo.toml: changed by 11 merged tasks of 11 engineers in 14 days
- Cargo.lock: changed by 6 merged tasks of 6 engineers in 14 days
- docs/RELEASING.md: changed by 6 merged tasks of 6 engineers in 14 days
- .github/workflows/release.yml: changed by 5 merged tasks of 5 engineers in 14 days
- CHANGELOG.md: changed by 4 merged tasks of 4 engineers in 14 days
- justfile: changed by 4 merged tasks of 4 engineers in 14 days
- src/gamma.rs: changed by 4 merged tasks of 4 engineers in 14 days
- .gitignore: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days
- data/io.github.cosmic_ext.Nightlight.desktop: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days
- docs/BUNDLED-ASSETS.md: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days
- scripts/publish-apt.sh: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days
- src/location.rs: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days
- src/solar.rs: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days

1. Measure. Check that list against the git history: the files changed most often and by the most different pieces of work, the files that change together, and why each keeps being edited (which kinds of change land in it).
2. Split. Where several kinds of work share a file, give each its own file, joined at compile time (a module of its own, its tests beside it). Where a file must know every kind of work (message dispatch, settings, event routing, a list of tests), make it a table or list that each part adds a line to from its own file, so adding a feature doesn't edit the shared one. Behaviour doesn't change: move code, don't rewrite it, keep every test passing, and commit in small steps.
3. Report. Say which files you split into which, and which of the list you left alone and why.

Leave generated and project-wide files (Cargo.lock, the README and the like) as they are. Stop at what the history justifies: a split of a file nobody keeps editing isn't worth making.

Second job: bring the project up to the Rust standards (RS1 to RS8, in your instructions as the rust-development skill; the project has no standards file of its own). The user gave no direction for this work: use the standards, the findings and the issues below.
No open issue from Compliance is about structure.

a. Measure first. Run the rust_smells tool on the whole tree (whole: true) and keep its counts: oversized files and impls, types spread over many impl blocks, fields always borrowed apart, borrow-ending clones, mem::take across calls, allocations in loops, unsafe. These are your "before" numbers. Read the project's requirements and contract too: they bind what you change.
b. Pin down behaviour before you move anything (RS6): the project's tests where they pin the results, and for code whose output you restructure, a check that old and new give the same output on fixed inputs, with iteration order made deterministic. Delete the old code once they match.
c. Reorganize toward the standards, most measured payoff first, in small commits: one large state struct into disjoint sub-structs, each with the impl that owns it (RS1, RS7); a kind field and a long if chain back into an enum or trait (RS3); clones that only ended a borrow removed by reshaping the data (RS1); a large crate split only where the measured incremental check time (cargo check after a one-line edit, before and after) gains. Move code, don't rewrite it: behaviour doesn't change and every test still passes. Don't split a file by line count alone, and leave generated files alone.
d. Measure again. Run rust_smells on the whole tree once more for your "after" numbers.

Your closing report_status says which standards (RS1 to RS8) the project now meets, which remain and why each does, with the scan's counts before and after, side by side.

Your closing report_status is published as your report, in the project's Reports tab (Architecture): put which files you divided up and why in its summary and decisions, and what changed in its files. Engineers start only once your work is merged. If nothing is worth dividing, commit nothing, say why, and say plainly in its summary that you have nothing left to do; an interim report_status doesn't end your turn's work. Once your work is merged (or you finish with nothing to merge), you're discarded.

[Ferrivide] A scan of your change to Rust files found 1 smell the Rust standards (the rust-development skill) cover. Fix what you agree is a problem, or say in your closing report why it stays; this note comes once for each.
- src/worker.rs:46 [loop-allocation] `handle_request` is called inside a loop in `spawn`, and does `Vec::new` through `GammaBackend::new` (src/gamma.rs:324) on every call (fix: RS4. Hot paths allocate nothing; see RS4)

understanding.request: As one-off architect: (1) measure which files agents keep editing and why, split those where several kinds of work share a file so parallel engineers touch different files, behaviour unchanged; (2) bring the code toward RS1–RS8, measuring rust_smells before and after; report what was split, what was left and why.
assumptions: The existing unit tests pin the pure logic; since code is moved verbatim (not restructured), the same tests passing plus a diff of moved lines is the RS6 check
The applet cannot be run on a live panel here, so no change that alters control flow (e.g. nested per-feature message enums) is made
plan: Baseline: cargo test --locked (47 passed, 1 ignored), rust_smells whole tree (1 finding: loop-allocation at src/main.rs:78, a documented false positive)

Split src/main.rs (1191 lines, over RS7's ~1000, edited by every feature: worker, popup, temperature, schedule, auto, settings) into worker.rs, schedule.rs, auto.rs, switch.rs, config.rs, popup.rs and app.rs, each with its own tests; main.rs keeps only mod lines, APP_ID and main()
Move code verbatim; only visibility (pub(crate)) and imports change
Run tests (same 47 names must pass), fmt, clippy; re-run rust_smells; commit in steps; report
out_of_scope: README.md, Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, CHANGELOG.md, justfile, .gitignore: project-wide or generated, cannot be usefully divided
release.yml, docs/RELEASING.md, scripts/publish-apt.sh: one kind of work (the release design reworked by successive tasks), not several kinds sharing a file
src/gamma.rs, solar.rs, location.rs: each one responsibility, under size limits, few edits
Splitting the crate: about 2,200 lines, no check-time gain to be had

files.why: Nightlight, AutoState, Message and the cosmic::Application impl, moved from main.rs
Config keys, config(), Settings load and save, and their tests
Now only the module list, APP_ID, main() and #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
popup_content, time_picker, temperature_hint, popup_after_close and their tests
TimeOfDay, Schedule, schedule_step, schedule_last_after_reply, local_time_of_day and their tests
toggle_request, applied, Retune, retune_on_slider, retune_needed and their tests
Gamma worker thread and handle_request, moved from main.rs

decisions.decision: Split src/main.rs by responsibility into seven modules, moving code verbatim
decisions.why: History shows every feature (worker, popup, temperature slider, schedule, auto mode, settings test) landed in main.rs: 18 commits, and it was over RS7's ~1000 lines. Pure logic, settings, popup layout and the worker now change in separate files. Checked by the same 47 test names passing and a line-by-line comparison of old and new sources (only visibility, imports and rustfmt wrapping differ).
alternatives: Spreading impl Nightlight across the feature files (RS7 names this as not helping)

decisions.decision: Kept Message, the Nightlight state and update() as one enum, one struct and one match in app.rs
decisions.why: Turning them into per-feature sub-messages and sub-states would rewrite control flow, and the applet has never been run on a live panel, so there is no way here to confirm behaviour is unchanged. A new feature therefore still adds lines to app.rs, popup.rs and config.rs; fixes to one feature's logic no longer collide.
alternatives: Nested per-feature message enums with their own update functions

decisions.decision: Left src/gamma.rs, solar.rs and location.rs as they are
decisions.why: Each has one responsibility and is well under the size limits (534, 252, 188 lines). gamma.rs's 4 edits were the backend's own build-out and the slider's temperature constants; solar.rs and location.rs had 2 each, from one feature and a format pass.
alternatives: Moving the colour-temperature maths out of gamma.rs

decisions.decision: Left README.md, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, CHANGELOG.md, justfile, .gitignore, the desktop file, docs/BUNDLED-ASSETS.md alone
decisions.why: Project-wide or generated. Cargo.toml's edits were dependencies, version and cargo-deb metadata, which cargo-deb reads only from Cargo.toml. The others had 2 to 4 small edits.

Their edits are one kind of work: the release process redesigned several times by successive tasks (tag push, then main push, signing, apt). Already split into build, attach and apt jobs; dividing the file would not have kept those tasks apart.

decisions.decision: Did not change the code behind the remaining RS4 scan finding
decisions.why: handle_request creates the backend only while it is None, once per connection; an earlier session already documented this in its comment. Reshaping it to quiet the scan would be a rewrite with no gain.
RS8: the crate has no unsafe, so it says so.

decisions.decision: No crate split and no check-time measurement
decisions.why: The crate is about 2,200 lines; there is no incremental check time to win.

progress: Split src/main.rs (1191 lines, edited by 12 tasks) into worker.rs, schedule.rs, auto.rs, switch.rs, config.rs, popup.rs and app.rs, code moved verbatim, each with its own tests; added #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. Same 47 tests pass, fmt and clippy clean. Not run on a live panel. rust_smells before → after: 1 → 1 finding (loop-allocation 1 → 1, a false positive now at src/worker.rs:46); oversized files 0 → 0 by the scan (main.rs was 1191 lines, the largest file is now gamma.rs at 534), borrow-ending clones 0 → 0, mem::take across calls 0 → 0, unsafe 0 → 0. Standards: RS1, RS2, RS3, RS5, RS6, RS7, RS8 met; RS4 has the one scan finding left, which is not a real hot-path allocation (GammaBackend::new runs once per connection, not per request). Every other file on the list was left alone. Nothing left for me to do once this is merged.

reviews.summary: The change cleanly separates applet responsibilities into focused modules, preserves the existing behavior and test coverage, and adds a crate-level unsafe prohibition. `cargo check --locked`, formatting checks, and the full test suite pass. No clear defects found in this quick review.

learned: Applet: src/main.rs is now only the module list. What earlier notes place in src/main.rs lives in: worker.rs (gamma worker thread), schedule.rs (TimeOfDay, Schedule, schedule_step), auto.rs (auto_percent_now, auto_action), switch.rs (toggle_request, applied, Retune), config.rs (config keys, Settings), popup.rs (popup_content, popup_after_close, time_picker), app.rs (Nightlight state, Message, update, init). A new feature still adds to app.rs, popup.rs and config.rs.
Applet: rust_smells reports one loop-allocation at handle_request in src/worker.rs. It is a false positive: GammaBackend::new runs only while the backend is None, once per connection.
summary:
This finding stays, and nothing changes in the code. It is the same one the scan reported before the split (then at `src/main.rs:78`); it only moved to `src/worker.rs:46` with the code.

It is not a real hot-path allocation:

- **Not on every call:** `handle_request` calls `GammaBackend::new` only while the backend is `None`, which is once per Wayland connection. Later requests reuse the cached backend.
- **Not a hot loop:** the worker loop runs once per user or timer request (a toggle, a slider move, a 20-second tick), not per frame.
- **No allocation at that line anyway:** `Vec::new` does not allocate until something is pushed.

An earlier session already wrote this reasoning into the comment above `handle_request`. Reshaping the code just to quiet the scan would be a rewrite with no gain, against the "move, don't rewrite" rule for this job.

My closing report already records this under RS4, so the report stands as published: `src/main.rs` split into seven modules in commit `839996f43c`, 47 tests passing, and nothing left for me to do once it is merged.
